title: gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 on vLLM, DGX Spark
slug_note: The official MXFP4 weights on vLLM 0.32.0 on the Spark: 47 tok/s on one stream, behind llama.cpp (81.6) on the same weights.

variation.quant_detail: MXFP4, 13.76 GB (official safetensors; MoE experts in MXFP4 as OpenAI shipped them)
variation.revision_note: HF snapshot of openai/gpt-oss-20b served on the Spark during the 2026-11-04 test (offline from the local cache)

engine.config: vllm serve in the vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0 image, context 16,384, up to 4 sequences, half the memory pool

requirements.notes: Not measured. The lab run reserved half of the 128 GB pool (0.50 memory fraction), which is a reservation, not the model's need. 16 GB is OpenAI's stated footprint for the 20B.

steps.text: Run the command inside the vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0 image with --gpus all, host networking and your Hugging Face cache mounted.

measurements.method: openai_bench.py: streaming /v1/chat/completions, single stream, one warm-up discarded, fresh nonce per summarise prompt (cold prefill), decode = (completion_tokens-1)/(last-first token time), temperature 0.6, median of 3; summarise neutral filler (676-682-token prompt, 256-256 output tokens); SR-98 four-engine comparison (same bench script, same prompts, context 16,384 on every engine); vLLM 0.32.0 in vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0 (sha256:befccf0e7e40), command as shown

caveats: Measured on a DGX Spark (2026-11-04) as the vLLM leg of the SR-98 four-engine run: the same official MXFP4 weights ran at 81.6 tok/s on llama.cpp, 58.48 on Ollama, 47.2 here and 40.85 on SGLang (short summarise prompt, median of 3).
Run inside vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0 with the GPU, host networking and the Hugging Face cache mounted; weights were already in the cache, so the run was offline.
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.50 reserves half of the shared 128 GB pool up front; that is a reservation, not what the model needs.

sources.note: official model card and MXFP4 safetensors
